clue.text: Check sieve put in to soak

indicators.note: put in tells us the sieve word is placed inside the soaking word

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp in water to soften it
to sieve is to strain

explanation.surface: Someone checks a sieve before plunging it into water to soak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like inspecting the sieve, but it is the definition; ret is an old flax-processing word for soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a curb or limit, which is what restraint means.

clue.text: Low-frequency radiation requires a warning

explanation.surface: Infrared rays demand a caution signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the lowest-frequency visible light; a red light is also a stop signal or danger sign.

clue.text: Plant producing artificial stone

parts.note: sham means fake or artificial
rock is stone

explanation.surface: A garden ornament made of imitation stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a clover-like plant, the emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Dried fruit is seen in wet weather

indicators.note: seen in tells us the word is appears inside the weather word

parts.note: rain is wet weather
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dried fruit spotted lying out in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape.

clue.text: Stingo brewed for bars

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters are stirred up and mixed into something new

explanation.surface: Strong old ale is brewed for pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingo is an old word for strong ale; 'brewed' rearranges its letters. 'bars' looks like pubs but means metal blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingots are bars of cast metal such as gold.

clue.text: What litigants bring to obtain a portmanteau judgment?

definitions.text: What litigants bring to obtain a portmanteau judgment?

parts.words: What litigants bring to obtain a portmanteau judgment?
parts.note: a portmanteau is a suitcase, so a ruling on one sounds like trying a bag; really it is a lawsuit whose decision sets a precedent for many others

explanation.surface: Legal parties seeking a ruling that covers a range of matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action whose outcome serves as a precedent for similar disputes.

clue.text: To sleep in it is not fitting

indicators.note: in says the sleeping word sits inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: Dozing off in it would be improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt describes something unsuitable or out of place.

clue.text: How a news scoop is broadcast without delay

definitions.text: How a news scoop is broadcast

explanation.surface: Breaking news going out on air at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgent news goes out as a bulletin flash; the phrase also means instantly.

clue.text: A priest needs assistance if apprehensive

parts.note: Fr is short for Father, a title for a priest
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: A cleric needs help when he is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid means fearful or worried.

clue.text: Continue to look after connective tissue

parts.note: to tend is to look after
on as in go on, continue

explanation.surface: Keep caring for an injured ligament.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a cord of tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Large number going to London borough for business

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: A big sum of money heads to a London suburb on commercial matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large number' looks like a lot of something, but it is just the Roman numeral D; EALING is a borough of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing is trade or commerce, the conduct of business.

clue.text: No longer held without consideration

explanation.surface: Something released from the grip, dismissed without thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a thing no longer in someone's grasp; idiomatically, rejecting something at once, with no thought given.

clue.text: Reasons for using a coffee-strainer

explanation.surface: Explaining why one uses a coffee filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are justifications for an action; they are also the dregs of brewed coffee caught by a strainer.

clue.text: Leave the radio playing martial music

parts.note: martial music is played by a military band, so a band supplies it
a radio that is playing is switched on

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a room where the radio is blaring military marches.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A BAND ON: a military band is on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something behind for good is to forsake it.

clue.text: Be struck by court shoes and make a fast exit

parts.note: to take to something is to be attracted by or struck with it
court shoes are women's plain high-heeled shoes, so one's heels

explanation.surface: Someone falls for a pair of court shoes and dashes off in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Court shoes are the British name for plain women's pumps with a heel.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee quickly, showing one's heels to the pursuer, is to run off at speed.

clue.text: Court hearing about traditional Good Friday fare

indicators.note: about says the hearing word goes round the food word

parts.note: a trial is a legal hearing
hot cross buns are traditionally eaten on Good Friday

explanation.surface: A court session concerning hot cross buns.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot cross buns are spiced, cross-marked buns eaten in Britain on Good Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that sits in judgment, like a court.

clue.text: Chum from Cathay

explanation.surface: A friend from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so old china is an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Old china is cockney slang for a pal; it is also, literally, the old name for the land called Cathay.

clue.text: Work out tax cut with hesitation

indicators.note: cut with says the tax word is split and the hesitation word set into it

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Calculating a reduced duty while dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to do physical training.

clue.text: Street surrounded with wire

parts.note: ringed means encircled

explanation.surface: A road fenced in by wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument is fitted with strings, often of wire.

clue.text: Monarch joined forces and returned to the fray

parts.note: R is short for Rex or Regina, king or queen
allied means joined forces with another party

explanation.surface: A king formed an alliance and went back into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops that rallied regrouped and came back to fight.

clue.text: Account for a loud explosion

explanation.surface: Describing a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a description of events; it is also the bang of a gun.

clue.text: Don't rush away from a festival in Germany

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Stay on at a German beer festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on, reluctant to leave, is to dawdle.

clue.text: Refrain from describing an ancestor

explanation.surface: Holding back from talking about one's forefather.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back from doing something is to forbear; forbear is also a variant spelling of forebear, a forefather.

clue.text: Conventional marines break in a young horse

indicators.note: break in tells us the marines word is set inside the horse word

parts.note: a foal is a young horse
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Soldiers tame a colt in the customary way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break in' reads as taming a young horse, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal means following accepted rules and etiquette.

clue.text: Putting one's oar in when having an argument

explanation.surface: Interfering in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally propelling a boat with oars; as a noun-like verb, rowing is quarrelling.

clue.text: Clerk gives a pound to drug peddler

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen
a pusher sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An office worker hands a pound coin to a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but is an animal enclosure, a PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging term for an office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Injuring Frenchman by pointing a gun

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a French title for a man
aiming is pointing a weapon at a target

explanation.surface: Someone hurts a Frenchman by levelling a rifle at him.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiming is wounding so as to cause lasting harm.

clue.text: Two apprentices in yodelling country

parts.note: a tyro is a novice or apprentice
L is the learner plate sign, marking an apprentice driver

explanation.surface: A pair of trainees in the Alpine region.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two different words for a beginner: TYRO, and L for learner, from the British L-plate shown by learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy famous for yodelling.

clue.text: Large lead translated into unanimous approval

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big lead is converted into a consensus.
explanation.definitionFit: When everyone consents there is complete agreement.
